summary: A vault owner's own settings: the profile record, how dates and numbers read, a change-password path both kinds share, a read-only main currency, dimension configuration, session listing and the idle lock, and self-service account deletion.

read.role: owns the idle-lock behaviour this screen sets the period for, the sessions rows an unlock leaves unchanged, the upgrade a password change makes redundant and which writes the held credential, and the expired-session handling a password changed elsewhere ends in
the store the profile record lives in

the account records that read the dimension ids configured here

profilePayload.value: { mainCurrency required, createdAt required, idleLockMinutes optional, one of the offered periods, with absent meaning 15, locale optional BCP 47 with absent or unrecognized meaning the browser's and never validated against a list, dateStyle optional one of locale dmy ymd mdy, groupSeparator optional one of locale thin apostrophe comma period none, moneyPlaces optional string one of locale 0 2 with locale meaning two, dimensions optional with absent or empty meaning none }. Registration writes the two required keys and nothing else, and each optional key appears the first time the user sets it

profileSingleton.value: one profile record per vault, the only record guaranteed to exist after registration. The API enforces no singleton, and clients treat the highest version as authoritative

oneFormatter.value: every figure and date reaches the screen through one formatter built from the profile, answering money at moneyPlaces for a figure in any currency (the main currency, and a holding's own unit whose symbol-table kind is currency), whole, percent(value, places), compact, quantity for a figure in any other unit, parseQuantity, editable(value, places) for a rate, parseFigure, date, and parseDate. money, whole, percent and compact each take a value exact at scale 12 and round it half-even. editable rounds nothing (editableEntry). parseDate returns nothing rather than guessing: a two-digit year and an impossible date are refused. Defaults are read from Intl at run time, never tabulated. A groupSeparator equal to the locale's decimal point is not applied (clashingGroupSeparator). No setting writes any record but the profile

clashingGroupSeparator.value: the decimal point is always the locale's, because no setting chooses it. A groupSeparator equal to that point is not applied, because 1.234 would then mean two things, and the locale's own group mark is in force instead. The point is never swapped to make room for the chosen mark, because that would change how every figure reads and which input a field accepts. Read at run time from Intl, never tabulated

clashExamples.value: locale en-US, groupSeparator period: money writes 1234567.89 as 1,234,567.89 (the locale's comma stands), parseQuantity reads 12.5 as "12.5" and refuses 12,5. Locale de-DE, groupSeparator comma: money writes 1234567.89 as 1.234.567,89. Product wording: with main currency CHF, figures read CHF 1,234,567.89

figureMinus.value: every figure entry writes a negative with the true minus, −, decided on the figure as written, so a value that rounds to zero carries no sign

wholeEntry.value: a summary figure in the main currency, in whole units, grouped and pointed as configured, used only where the screen file names one. spec/ui/dashboard.md, Hero figure, names the total, the change, gross assets and liabilities, the legend and the breakdown

percentEntry.value: percent(value, places) writes a percentage at places, grouped and pointed as configured, followed by % with no space. value is already the percentage, so 12.5 writes 12.5%. It does not follow moneyPlaces, because a percentage keeps the places its caller asks for

percentExamples.value: locale de-DE, groupSeparator period, percent at one place: 136794.6 writes 136.794,6% under moneyPlaces 0 and 2 alike, 0.25 writes 0,2%, 0.35 writes 0,4%, -0.25 writes −0,2%, -0.04 writes 0,0%. At no places -50 writes −50%. Locale de-CH, groupSeparator apostrophe, one place: 10957493 writes 10’957’493.0%

compactEntry.value: a value tick on the trend chart, in the short form spec/features/net-worth-view.md, Value ticks, defines, grouped and pointed as configured

compactExamples.value: locale de-DE, groupSeparator apostrophe: 999 writes 999, 1500 writes 1,5k, 2000000 writes 2M, -2500000 writes −2,5M, 1500000000000 writes 1’500B

noScreenWritesAFigure.value: a screen adds only words, a unit or currency code, and the sign of a signed change. Its digits, group marks, decimal point, rounding, minus and percent sign are what a formatter entry returns. A figure written with toFixed, toLocaleString, Intl.NumberFormat, String of a number or a template string skips every setting. No client module but the formatter's calls toFixed, toLocaleString or Intl.NumberFormat

dateWriters.value: date and parseDate serve a date field and nothing else. Dates shown for reading go through one writer per slot: longDate (day, abbreviated month, year: a sentence, a row, a tooltip, a table), fullDate (month in full, for a heading), dayMonth (day and month, long or abbreviated, for a label that implies the year), monthYear (month in full and year) and dateTime (a moment in the browser's time zone: longDate, a comma, hours and minutes in the locale's form). Under dateStyle locale they spell the month in the locale's language. Under dmy, ymd or mdy every writer but monthYear writes the whole date in that style, the text date writes, and dayMonth writes the year too. monthYear keeps its spelling under every style

dateWriterExamples.value: en-US, no dateStyle, 2026-09-20: date 09/20/2026, longDate Sep 20, 2026, fullDate September 20, 2026, dayMonth September 20 and Sep 20, monthYear September 2026, dateTime starting Sep 20, 2026, . en-US, dateStyle dmy: date, longDate, fullDate and both dayMonth forms 20.09.2026, dateTime starting 20.09.2026, , monthYear September 2026. The settings sample line writes its date with longDate

quantityFormat.value: a stored value in any unit that is not a currency (a metal or free text) is shown digit for digit from its decimal string: never rounded, never padded, the group mark in force between groups of three in the integer part and the locale's decimal point. "12.125" reads 12.125, "12.50" reads 12.50 and "80" reads 80. It does not follow moneyPlaces. It formats a stored string and nothing computed. A negative value is signed as money is. The same rule holds as text and in a field, on every screen

parseQuantity.value: the reverse of quantity, for a field. The locale's decimal point is the point, and so is . wherever . is not the group mark in force. The group mark in force is accepted only between groups of three digits in the integer part, and anywhere else the input is malformed, never dropped, because 12.5 read as 125 under a period group mark is a silent tenfold error. Returns the canonical decimal string or nothing

editableEntry.value: editable(value, places) writes a rate wherever one is written: in its field, in the note naming the figure an edit replaced, beside a rival entry, and in a recording's price column. Every digit of the exact value is kept, never rounded, and the fraction is padded to at least places, grouped and pointed as configured and signed as money is. A rate takes six places, because a currency pair moves in the fourth. It does not follow moneyPlaces, because a price is not money

editableExamples.value: 0.797 writes 0.797000, 0.9312 writes 0.931200, 0.93124567 writes 0.93124567, and a proposal at eight places writes all eight. Locale de-DE, groupSeparator apostrophe: "1234.56789" writes 1’234,567890 and "0.12345678" writes 0,12345678

parseFigure.value: the reverse of editable, for a rate field. It reads as parseQuantity does and returns the exact value at scale 12, or nothing

ratePrefill.value: a rate field prefills through editable at six places and compares by value, never by text. Its parseFigure reading equals the stored or proposed rate whenever padding is all that differs, so an untouched line writes nothing and keeps its provenance. This differs from a stored value's prefill, which goes through quantity

canonicalDecimalString.value: -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]{1,12})?, a zero carrying no sign. Defined by record-snapshot.md and returned by parseQuantity

editPrefill.value: a field that edits a stored figure prefills it through quantity, whatever the unit, money included, because a prefill at moneyPlaces saved untouched would write the rounding. A field whose text still equals its prefill is untouched and is never parsed, so it saves the stored string itself

changePasswordEndpoint.value: POST /api/auth/change-password { currentAuthKey, salt, kdf, authKey, wrappedDek, dekNonce }. The server verifies currentAuthKey against the stored hash, then replaces the password credential row's params and verifier and, for a vault owner, that credential's one dek_wrappers row, in one transaction. No other row is written

changePasswordWrongCurrentAuthKey.value: a mismatch of currentAuthKey against the stored hash is a Bad Request with no refused member, and writes nothing

heldCredential.value: a vault owner's tab holds the password credential's salt, KDF envelope, wrappedDek and dekNonce as one set, from the sign-in, unlock or registration that opened the vault. The unwrap in step 2 uses it, and a failed unwrap means a wrong current password: nothing is sent, a salt lookup included. Every flow that rewrites any of them replaces the held copy with what it sent, once the server answers OK: the stale-KDF upgrade, a password change, and an import's re-key (wrapper alone). A lock discards the set with the keys and the unlock that follows fills it again. An administrator's tab holds the salt and envelope the same way

wrongCurrentPasswordRequests.value: a vault owner's wrong current password sends no request of any kind. An administrator's request is sent and the server answers Bad Request. The error text is "That is not your current password."

noSaltRequestOnSuccess.value: a successful change sends no /api/auth/salt request: the first after sign-in, a second from the same tab, one after that tab's stale-KDF upgrade, one after that tab's import, and one after a lock and unlock (the unlock's own request excepted)

credentialUpgradedElsewhereRetry.value: when another live session ran the stale-KDF upgrade, AK_old from the held salt fails with Bad Request. The client looks up /api/auth/salt once. If its salt or envelope differs from the held one, it re-derives currentAuthKey from the fresh pair and resends once, unchanged apart from currentAuthKey. The held set stays as it was until the change succeeds. An unchanged pair, or a second Bad Request, is final: a vault owner sees the change-failed error, an administrator the wrong-password one. One retry, never a loop. Observable as one /api/auth/salt request and two change-password requests

passwordChangedElsewhere.value: a password change on another session ended this session, so the request answers Unauthorized (401) whatever it carries, and the client treats it as any expired session (login.md, Edge cases). The unlock that follows looks the new salt up, so the stale held set never reaches a request

changePasswordComparesEpoch.value: for a vault owner the transaction compares the vault epoch after BEGIN IMMEDIATE and before any write, because a page holding a DEK an import replaced would otherwise wrap the old key under the new password and leave every record unreadable. A replaced epoch answers Conflict {"refused":"vault-replaced"} with a correct currentAuthKey, and credentials, dek_wrappers and sessions stay as they were, so the restored vault still opens with the unchanged password. An administrator has no epoch and the header on their request is ignored

deleteAccountComparesEpoch.value: DELETE /api/auth/account compares the vault epoch after BEGIN IMMEDIATE, so a page that confirmed deleting a vault since replaced deletes nothing. A replaced epoch with a correct authKey and confirmUsername answers Conflict {"refused":"vault-replaced"} and deletes nothing

deleteAccountDeletesTheEpoch.value: account deletion removes the principal row, every credential row, every wrapper, every record, the vault epoch and every session in one transaction. It leaves no vault_epochs row for the account

importEndsNoSession.value: an import ends no session. A password change alone ends every other session and keeps the current one, and log out everywhere ends every session including the current one

changePasswordDerivesAtCurrentParameters.value: the client derives the new keys with the server's current default KDF parameters read from the envelope the app shell embeds, not the old ones. A password change is also a KDF upgrade

changePasswordBar.value: at least 12 characters and zxcvbn at least 3, the same bar as registration

changePasswordByKind.value: the server discriminates on the session's principal kind and not on which fields arrived, so a vault owner's request without a wrapper is a Bad Request and an administrator's with one is too. An administrator sends no wrapper and their current password is verified server-side only, because the second check was the unwrap and there is nothing to unwrap

changePasswordSessions.value: invalidates all other sessions for the account and keeps the current one. The client keeps its in-memory DEK and no re-login is needed

disabledConfirmLook.value: Delete my vault is disabled until the password is filled and the typed username matches, in the one disabled look every primary, secondary and destructive button shares: petrol-200 fill and border, label ink-secondary at 5.24:1, no hover change, cursor default, no opacity, and no critical red, so it turns red only once it can act

noRemovePassword.value: there is no remove-password action and there will not be one. Changing the password replaces the row, and nothing deletes it short of deleting the account

exportWarning.value: the screen must warn that existing export files still open with the old password, since they carry their own salt and wrapped DEK

mainCurrencyIsReadOnly.value: displayed, not editable in v1, with a one-line note that it is fixed at registration and why. Import is the one exception, and it is not a loophole, because it replaces the price history along with the profile

dimensionsShape.value: a list of { id, label, archivedAt, values: [{ id, label, archivedAt }] }

dimensionIdFormat.value: 8 characters of [a-z0-9] from crypto.getRandomValues, minted at creation, checked for uniqueness against the profile already in memory. Each character is drawn uniformly from the 36 by rejection: a random value outside the range is redrawn, never reduced modulo 36. Opaque and immutable, never shown, never typed, never derived from the label

dimensionOrder.value: order in values is the band order in the stacked chart, and order of dimensions is the order of the dashboard's Group by select. Reordering writes one record

deletingIsArchiving.value: deleting a dimension or a single value sets archivedAt and keeps the definition in the profile, leaving every account's dims entry untouched. There is no remove-everywhere option and no multi-record write anywhere in this feature

flagShape.value: a dimension with a single value is the shape that replaces a yes/no tag, and the account form renders it as a checkbox rather than a select. Absence of an entry means no

valuesBeyondFour.value: values may exceed four and the chart folds the remainder into Other. The screen says so rather than capping the list, because the limit is a rendering constraint and not a data one

deleteAccountEndpoint.value: DELETE /api/auth/account { authKey, confirmUsername }. The server checks authKey against the stored hash in constant time and that confirmUsername equals the session user's normalized username. A mismatch on either is a Bad Request and deletes nothing. It deletes the principal row, every credential row, every wrapper, every record, the vault epoch and every session in one transaction, with nothing soft-deleted

deleteAccountHasNoAdministratorGuard.value: no last-administrator check, because a vault owner is never an administrator. The dialog offers export first as the primary action and deletion as the secondary one

idleLock.value: user-configurable, default 15, stored as idleLockMinutes in the encrypted profile record, so it follows the user across devices and the server never sees it. Absent means 15. No setting disables it. There is no idle rule for an administrator. A changed period applies at once, not from the next activity

idleLockOfferedPeriods.value: 5, 10, 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes, with 15 selected on a vault that has never set it

idleLockStoredValueRule.value: any other stored number, a fraction included, locks at the nearest offered period and the shorter on a tie, and the select shows that period. A stored value that is not a number means 15. Stored 0, 500, 7 and 7.5 lock at 5, 60, 5 and 5

sessionExpiry.value: absolute, 12 hours from issue, for both kinds. login.md, Rules owns the value

sessionEndpoints.value: POST /api/auth/logout invalidates the current session, with the client discarding its in-memory keys first, and answers OK without a session. POST /api/auth/logout-all invalidates every session for the user including the current one, and there is no all-except-this-one variant. GET /api/sessions returns [{ id, issuedAt, lastActiveAt, current }], where id is an opaque handle and never the cookie's value

sessionsListOnlyLive.value: GET /api/sessions lists only live sessions, meaning not past the absolute expiry. An expired row is left off whether or not a sign-in has deleted it yet. It returns only the session user's own sessions

sessionListFetchTriggers.value: the page fetches GET /api/sessions when it renders, on Retry, and again once a change-password response is OK, with no navigation between. After the change the Open sessions table shows skeleton rows while it reloads, then the one row marked This session. A failed fetch, that one included, replaces the rows with the card's load error and Retry and leaves none of the earlier rows in view. Password changed also shows the inline confirmation under Change password

unlockAddsNoSession.value: unlocking signs in on the same server session and adds no row. Locking and unlocking leaves GET /api/sessions with the same entries, the same id and the same issuedAt. This screen owns only the idle period

noSessionMetadata.value: no IP address and no user-agent is stored in a session row, and no endpoint returns any, because none is recorded. The one trace of a connection is the attempts table's keyed address key from a failed sign-in, which GET /api/sessions never returns and which cannot be read back without SECRET_KEY (spec/architecture.md#storage-data-handling)

openSessionsNotice.value: Solvent keeps no IP address readable and records no devices.

wrongCurrentAuthKeyOrConfirmUsername.condition: checked server-side, since a client bypassing the dialog is the case that matters (spec/features/account-settings.md#delete-my-account)

wrongCurrentAuthKeyOnChangePassword.condition: currentAuthKey does not match the stored hash; no refused member, nothing written (spec/features/account-settings.md#change-password)

passwordChangedOnAnotherSession.condition: a change-password request from a session the other session's change ended (spec/features/account-settings.md#edge-cases)

vaultReplaced.condition: a vault owner's change-password or account-deletion request carrying the epoch from before an import. The body is {"refused":"vault-replaced"} and nothing is written (spec/features/account-settings.md#acceptance-criteria)

changePasswordWrapperMismatch.condition: an administrator session carrying a wrapper, or a vault owner session without one (spec/features/account-settings.md#change-password)

fixtures: a vault holding records written before a password change, decrypted again afterwards in the same session and after a fresh login
a seeded administrator session, for the four Not Found assertions and for the administrator change-password path

a vault owner session holding the epoch from before an import, a correct currentAuthKey, a correct authKey and a matching confirmUsername, for the two vault-replaced assertions and the credentials, dek_wrappers, sessions and records captured before and after
a vault owner with a vault_epochs row, deleted through the endpoint, for the no-epoch-row assertion
a second session for the same user, for the invalidate-others-keep-current assertion and for POST /api/auth/logout

request logs of /api/auth/salt and /api/auth/change-password from one tab, for the no-salt-request and one-salt-two-change assertions across: first change after sign-in, a second change, a change after the tab's stale-KDF upgrade, after its import, and after a lock and unlock
a second live session that signs in after the first tab opened its vault and runs the stale-KDF upgrade, for the credential-upgraded-elsewhere retry
a second session that changes the password while the first tab stays open, for the Unauthorized assertion and the unlock that follows
a sessions row past the absolute expiry and not yet deleted, and another user's live session, for the GET /api/sessions listing assertions
a lock and unlock on a live session, with GET /api/sessions captured before and after

a second session open for the same user before the first page changes its password, and a way to make the GET /api/sessions that follows the change fail, for the two Open sessions assertions after a change
a vault stored at KDF parameters below the server default, for the assertion that a password change lands at the current default
hand-built requests that skip the dialog entirely: change-password with a wrong currentAuthKey, and DELETE /api/auth/account with a wrong authKey and with a mismatched confirmUsername
profile records carrying idleLockMinutes of 0, 500, 7, 7.5 and a non-number, for the nearest-offered-period assertion
locale de-DE with groupSeparator period, under moneyPlaces 0 and 2, and locale de-CH with groupSeparator apostrophe and moneyPlaces 0, for the percent cases in percentExamples
locale de-DE with groupSeparator apostrophe, for the compact cases in compactExamples
the client source tree, scanned for toFixed, toLocaleString and Intl.NumberFormat outside the formatter module
locale en-US with no dateStyle, and with dateStyle dmy, and the date 2026-09-20 with a moment on that day, for the date writer assertions
a profile with no dimensions key at all, for the Total-only dashboard

locale de-DE with groupSeparator apostrophe and moneyPlaces 0 and 2, with rates "0.797", "0.9312", "0.93124567", "1234.56789" and "0.12345678", for the editable cases in editableExamples, plus a rate field prefilled from a stored rate and saved untouched, with the record captured before and after

profile records carrying each value of dateStyle, groupSeparator and moneyPlaces, a locale tag this engine does not know, and a groupSeparator equal to the locale's decimal point, for the formatter assertions
locale en-US with groupSeparator period, and locale de-DE with groupSeparator comma, for the clash cases in clashExamples

main currency CHF, groupSeparator apostrophe and moneyPlaces 0, with a USD holding valued 1000.40, an XAU-ozt holding stored as "12.125", another stored as "12.50" and an m² holding stored as "80", for the unit-kind formatter assertion

locale de-DE and groupSeparator apostrophe with an m² holding stored as "1234.5", for the quantity display and the parseQuantity cases 1’234,50 and 12.5; locale de-DE and groupSeparator period for the cases 1.234,5 and 12.5 (the last refused)

locale de-CH and moneyPlaces 0, with a past snapshot of a USD holding stored as "1000.40" and one of an XAU-ozt holding stored as "12.125", for the edit-dialog prefill assertions, with the stored record captured before and after a note-only edit
a profile with an archived dimension and an archived value, plus accounts carrying entries that name them, with every account record captured before and after for byte comparison
focus: the disabled Delete my vault must be asserted on computed style, disabled and then enabled: petrol-200 fill and border, ink-secondary label, opacity 1, no red while disabled, red once the password is filled and the username matches. A button dimmed with opacity or left red passes a test of the disabled attribute alone

the change-password transaction must be shown to write nothing but the password credential row and its own wrapper, with every record's ciphertext byte-identical afterwards. Counting requests is not the same as comparing rows, and a re-encryption of records would pass every functional test while costing exactly what the DEK indirection exists to save

a change-password carrying the pre-import epoch with a correct currentAuthKey must answer vault-replaced and leave credentials, dek_wrappers and sessions as they were, and the restored vault must still open with the unchanged password. A server that skips the epoch wraps the old DEK under the new password and every record becomes unreadable, which only a restore-then-change sequence shows

the account deletion carrying the pre-import epoch must delete nothing with a correct authKey and confirmUsername, so a page that confirmed deleting a vault since replaced cannot destroy it, and a deletion that goes through must leave no vault_epochs row. Asserting the wrong-authKey refusal alone passes a deletion that never compares the epoch

the no-salt-request criteria must be asserted from the request log of the tab, across all five sequences (first change, second change, after stale-KDF upgrade, after import, after lock and unlock). A held set that is replaced only on some flows passes the first change and fails the next, and a fresh salt lookup on every change passes every functional test

the credential-upgraded-elsewhere case must be asserted as exactly one /api/auth/salt request and two change-password requests, with the second differing from the first only in currentAuthKey, and the new password then signing in. A retry loop or a resend that re-derives the new keys passes the sign-in half
a vault owner's wrong current password must send nothing between submit and the error, asserted from the request log, not from the message
a wrong currentAuthKey must be rejected server-side even with the client-side unwrap bypassed. The client check is the one an attacker skips, so the test has to call the endpoint directly

DELETE /api/auth/account must be called directly with a wrong authKey and with a mismatched confirmUsername. The typed username is a deliberate second factor of intent, and treating it as a UI formality passes every dialog-driven test

'no operation in the dimensions feature writes more than one record' must be asserted by counting PUT requests across create, rename, reorder, archive and restore, and by comparing every account record byte for byte. A multi-record write that happens to succeed is invisible otherwise
archiving a dimension and restoring it must return every account to its band with no account record written in either direction, which is the assertion that catches a tidy-up write

GET /api/sessions must be asserted against the endpoint's full response shape, so the test fails if an IP address or user-agent field is added later. Asserting the absence of a value is not the same as asserting the absence of a field

lock and unlock must be shown to leave GET /api/sessions with the same entries, the same id and the same issuedAt, compared before and after. An unlock that inserts a row or moves issuedAt looks identical from the screen

the Open sessions list after a password change must be asserted on the page that made the change, with a second session open beforehand and no navigation or reload, as one row marked This session. A list fetched only at render passes every test that reloads, and a client that hides the rows without fetching passes a screen check; the request log must show a GET /api/sessions after the OK response

a failed GET /api/sessions after a password change must leave the card's load error and Retry and none of the earlier rows. A card that keeps the stale rows under an error passes a test that only looks for the error text
an expired row not yet deleted must be absent from GET /api/sessions, asserted with the row still in the table. A listing that relies on a sign-in's cleanup passes every test that signs in first

the password change must keep the initiating session alive while killing every other one, asserted from both sides, because an implementation that kills all of them still passes the half of the criterion people write
the idle-lock setting must be shown to appear in plaintext nowhere in the database, which means scanning the stored rows rather than trusting that it went into the profile payload

the stored idle periods 0, 500, 7 and 7.5 must each be asserted by the period the lock fires at and by the value the select shows, with a changed period locking at the new one with no activity after the change. A select-only test passes an implementation that locks at the raw stored number, and 7.5 is the tie that shows the shorter side wins

each date writer must be asserted on a screen that shows a date, not on the formatter alone, under dateStyle locale and under dmy, with monthYear unchanged by the style. A screen that spells a month with date, or that writes digits with longDate, passes the formatter test
the formatter must be asserted on every screen that shows a figure, not on the formatter alone. A screen that formats a number itself passes every formatter test while ignoring the setting

percent must be asserted on the ties 0.25, 0.35 and -0.25 at one place and on -0.04, and under moneyPlaces 0 and 2 alike. A float or half-away rounding writes 0,3% for 0.25, and a sign decided before rounding writes -0,0% for -0.04, so both pass 136794.6

a groupSeparator that clashes with the locale's decimal point must be asserted both ways at once: en-US with period still writes 1,234,567.89 and parseQuantity still reads 12.5 and refuses 12,5, and de-DE with comma writes 1.234.567,89. An implementation that swaps the point to make room writes 1.234.567,89 for en-US, and one that drops the clashing mark with no fallback writes 1234567.89, so asserting only 'the period is not applied' passes both

compact must be asserted at 999, 1500, 2000000, -2500000 and 1500000000000 with the apostrophe group mark in force, because 1’500B is the only case where the group mark reaches a short form and the true minus reaches a negative one

the no-hand-formatting rule must be asserted by scanning the client source for toFixed, toLocaleString and Intl.NumberFormat outside the formatter, not by the formatter's own tests. A screen that formats a figure itself passes every formatter test

the USD and XAU-ozt holdings must each be asserted in both places their figure appears, with its unit and in the holding page's list of values. A formatter keyed on the main currency alone, or on moneyPlaces for every unit, passes the main-currency cases while rounding 12.125 ounces to 12 or padding 80 m² to 80.00

quantity display must be asserted with values that rounding or padding would change, "12.125", "12.50" and "80", under moneyPlaces 0 and under 2. A value like "12.5" or "3.00" passes a formatter that pads to two places

parseQuantity must be asserted on the refusal as well as the reading: 12.5 under a period group mark is refused, never read as 125. A parser that drops a misplaced group mark passes every accepted-input case

editable must be asserted with rates that rounding or short padding would change: "0.797" reads 0.797000, "0.93124567" and a twelve-place rate keep every digit, and the result is identical under moneyPlaces 0 and 2. A formatter that rounds to six passes 0.797 and loses the eighth place of a proposal, and one that follows moneyPlaces writes 1 for a franc-dollar rate

a rate line saved untouched must write no record and keep its provenance, asserted by loading a stored 0.9312 (padded in its field as 0.931200) and saving, with the stored record byte-identical afterwards. A field that compares by text sees 0.931200 against 0.9312 and restamps the entry as edited

the edit prefill must be shown by saving the dialog untouched and comparing the stored value string byte for byte. A dialog that prefills 1’000 for "1000.40" and parses it back on save looks identical until the record is read
